title: Phasor sum of the three series voltages
caption: In a series circuit the current is common. V_R (6 V) is in phase with it, V_L (12 V) leads by 90° and V_C (4 V) lags by 90°, so V_L and V_C point opposite ways and partly cancel to 8 V. The supply voltage is the vector sum: √(6² + 8²) = 10 V, ahead of the current by 53.1°, not the plain sum 22 V.
alt: Phasor diagram: V_R = 6 V to the right, V_L = 12 V up and V_C = 4 V down, with the supply voltage 10 V at 53.1 degrees above the current direction.
description: V_R = 6 V is drawn along the reference direction (the current).
V_L = 12 V is drawn up, 90° ahead; V_C = 4 V is drawn down, 90° behind.
Supply voltage = √(6² + 8²) = 10 V at 53.1° ahead of the current.

claims.name: the supply leads the current by 53.1°
